text: The Pont Serme, also known as the Pons Selinus and later the Pons Septimus, was a Roman bridge located on the Via Domitia in the Aude department, within the commune of Coursan in Occitania, southern France. Spanning approximately 1500 meters [1], the viaduct crossed the broad marshes of the Aude River and the Etang de Capestang, situated west of Béziers, and was longer than Trajan's Bridge over the Danube. Today, very little of the structure remains, with only its name surviving—now associated with a nearby wine estate called "Domaine de Pontserme" [2][3].
